title: pyrigor diagnostics v2
description: Output contract for pyrigor's diagnostics. This file defines the finding types.
x-root: No document validates yet, because the document wrapper is not defined.
Validate a single type through its definition, such as #/$defs/Finding.
x-extension-policy: pyrigor validates its own output strictly against this schema.
Consumers must ignore fields they do not know.
Adding an optional field is a compatible change.
Removing a field, or making an optional field required, changes the version.
Changing a field's type or meaning changes the version.
x-absent-values: Lists are always present. Only fixes may be empty.
Optional values are omitted when absent, never written as null.
x-invariants: byte_start is less than or equal to byte_end.
A span's start position is not after its end position.
Lines and columns agree with the byte offsets under the position conventions of Span.
No position falls inside a byte-order mark.
No position falls between the carriage return and the line feed of a CRLF.
Edits within a fix are sorted by byte_start and then byte_end.
Edits within a fix do not overlap, and no two zero-width edits share an offset.
Edits within a fix are all in the same file.
A finding's primary span is in the file the finding belongs to.
x-span-conventions: byte_start and byte_end are offsets into the raw bytes of the file, end-exclusive.
A UTF-8 byte-order mark counts 3 bytes, and a CRLF counts 2.
Lines break only on a line feed, a CRLF or a lone carriage return, where Python's parser breaks them.
Other characters, such as U+2028 or a form feed, are not line breaks.
Columns are 1-based Unicode code points, end-exclusive, and do not count a byte-order mark.
A line's break characters belong to the line they end.
The position just before a line break is on that line, after its last character.
The position just after a line break is column 1 of the next line.
The end of a file that ends with a line break is column 1 of the line after the last line.
The end of a file without a final line break is on the last line, after its last character.
A zero-width range, where byte_start equals byte_end, is allowed.
file_name is the path relative to the working directory, with forward slashes.

x-enclosing-symbol-conventions: The innermost definition that contains the finding.
The name is Python's __qualname__ for it, such as Class.method or outer.<locals>.inner.
At module level the name is <module> and the kind is module.
A function defined directly in a class body is a method.
Lambdas and comprehensions are not symbols, so the nearest enclosing definition is used.
x-fix-conventions: The edits of one fix are all in the same file, and apply together or not at all.
Edit offsets refer to the original file.
Edits are sorted by byte_start and then byte_end.
Overlapping ranges, and two zero-width edits at the same offset, are not allowed.
x-edit-conventions: byte_start and byte_end follow the byte conventions of Span.
A zero-width range inserts the content.

Finding.description: One concrete occurrence of a rule violation.

message.description: What was found, for a human reader.

spans.description: The source ranges involved. Exactly one is primary. Secondary spans may be in other files.

fixes.description: Alternative fixes. A consumer applies at most one of them.

allOf.description: Relative, so not starting with a slash or a drive letter.
No empty segment, and no trailing slash.

label.description: Why this range matters. Omitted when no explanation is needed.

EnclosingSymbol.description: Where a finding is. See x-enclosing-symbol-conventions.

allOf.description: <module>, or identifiers joined by dots, with <locals> only between two identifiers.

Fix.description: One way to resolve a finding. See x-fix-conventions.

applicability.description: Whether the fix may be applied automatically.

Edit.description: Replaces a byte range with content. See x-edit-conventions.
